description:
Over the trace the downlink reference signal received power was stable and strong, ranging from -78.0 dB to -73.0 dB. The mean RSRP was -77.2 dB.

Uplink modulation and coding showed a temporary degradation: UL_MCS fell to a low of 8 around t=26–41 but otherwise ranged between 8.0 and 18.0 with a mean of 16.5. Downlink MCS remained constant at 7.0. Uplink SNR stayed healthy, ranging from 14.7 dB to 26.2 dB with a mean of 21.0 dB.

BLERs were low on the downlink (0 to 0.032, mean 0.003) and higher and more variable on the uplink (0.022 to 0.15, mean 0.078), indicating more uplink retransmission risk than downlink.

Uplink resource allocation and utilization were bursty. UL_NPRB varied between 5.0 and 41.3 with a mean of 17.0 and experienced several pronounced jumps (largest spike raising it to 41.3). PRBs allocated on the uplink ranged from 0 to 29 with a mean near 1.7 and showed short spikes to ~28.6. UL PRB utilization mirrored that behavior: 0 to 27 (mean 1.6) with notable spikes. Downlink PRB allocation and utilization also had multiple large jumps, with PRBs_DL_Current spanning 0 to 67 (mean 18.9) and PRB_Utilization_DL spanning 0 to 64 (mean 17.8), including a major surge to ~67 PRBs and ~64% utilization late in the trace.

Traffic volumes and buffer occupancy were bursty. Transmitted bytes jumped to a maximum of 448,763 Bytes from a minimum of 0 Bytes, with a mean TX_Bytes of 107,196 Bytes. Received bytes ranged from 46 Bytes to 98,783 Bytes and averaged 6,250.2 Bytes, with several sharp spikes. The estimated uplink buffer ranged between 14.0 KB and 14,800.4 KB and averaged 503.8 KB, peaking in correspondence with uplink transmission bursts.

Packet counts reflected the bursty load: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0–86 (mean 33.5), DL_NumberOfPackets ranged 0–510 (mean 118.1). Protocol usage was predominantly TCP on both directions: DL traffic was TCP for 75.78% and UDP for 23.44% of timestamps; UL was TCP for 83.59% and UDP for 14.84%.

Overall, the trace shows good radio conditions (strong RSRP and solid UL_SNR) with intermittent uplink capacity and buffering spikes, higher uplink BLER than downlink, and periodic heavy PRB and byte bursts that drive buffer growth and short-lived increases in MCS variability.
